observed: One arched bell jar, top lifting loop and sealed baseplate, surrounding an open beaker on the left and a support stand on the right.
The beaker has a liquid surface below its rim and multiple hollow bubble marks below that surface.
A long thermometer-like instrument passes through a horizontal clamp into the beaker; its lower sensing part is submerged. The clamp joins the right-hand stand.
A base outlet descends below the plate, bends right and ends in a rightward arrow toward the pump. No heater, numerical temperature or pressure scale.
originalInventory.modern_mapping: Keep the jar/beaker containment, immersed thermometer, stand/clamp and rightward pump connection. English Bell jar/Thermometer/Water/To pump are identification additions. Bubble locations/count are illustrative, not a measurement or a claim that every liquid point nucleates at once. No child operation or exact pressure/temperature setting.
uncertainties: The instrument's small interior markings are not a readable scale and will not be supplied with invented values.
